memo_rationale: The lead-in makes even present-fact statements continuing promises. That conflicts with a risk-bearing purchase and converts later deterioration into breach. Separate funding-date facts from express operational covenants.
memo_replacement: Merchant makes each representation of existing fact in this Section as of the Effective Date and, after a reasonable opportunity to update its disclosures, the Purchase Date only. A representation is not a promise of future financial condition, revenue, solvency, or business continuity. Only a provision expressly stated as a continuing covenant applies after the Purchase Date. An inaccurate statement or covenant breach gives rise to remedies only as provided in Sections 6 and 9.
current_body: Merchant represents, warrants, and covenants that as of the Effective Date and during the term of this Agreement:
my_note: Structurally important and under-rated at High. The lead-in makes present-fact statements continuing promises, which is what turns ordinary business deterioration into breach and — via §9.2(b) — into personal liability. Fixing 045/047/085 without fixing this leaves the leak open.

heading: Unencumbered Receipts
memo_rationale: The absolute title warranty reaches unknown liens, statutory interests, equities, and every other possible adverse right. Combined with §9.2(b), an innocent error can become personal recourse. Require disclosure and reasonable inquiry, while making Buyer responsible for priority diligence.
memo_replacement: To Merchant’s knowledge after reasonable inquiry, Merchant is entitled to sell the Purchased Receipts and has disclosed to Buyer all known prior assignments and consensual liens affecting them. Section 1 shall identify any permitted prior interests and required releases or subordinations. Merchant does not warrant the absence of unknown statutory interests, processor rights, or legal claims. Buyer shall independently verify priority before funding. An inaccurate title statement creates liability under the Guaranty only if the conduct and proof requirements of Section 9.2 are satisfied.
current_body: Merchant has good, complete, and marketable title to all Receipts, free and clear of any and all liabilities, liens, claims, charges, restrictions, conditions, options, rights, mortgages, security interests, equities, pledges, and encumbrances of any kind or nature whatsoever, or any other rights or interests that may be inconsistent with the transactions contemplated with, or adverse to the interests of, Buyer, other than the monthly Equipment payment billed at merchant level by the Approved Processor under an Equipment Lease Agreement between Merchant and {{equipmentAffiliate}}, which is a permitted claim ranking after the Specified Percentage.
my_note: Rated High; it belongs with the blockers because of what §9.2(b) does to it. An absolute title warranty reaching unknown liens and statutory interests, made personally actionable, means an innocent error becomes personal recourse. Reasonable-inquiry standard, and Buyer owns priority diligence.

heading: Defaults under Other Contracts; Improper Transfers
memo_rationale: Merchant cannot reliably warrant judicial conclusions about fraudulent transfer, preferences, equitable subordination, or voidability “for any other reason.” These issues also depend on Buyer’s conduct and value. Replace with disclosure of known actual contractual restrictions; preserve bankruptcy defenses.
memo_replacement: Merchant has disclosed any known contractual restriction that would materially prevent the sale of Purchased Receipts or the agreed processor split. Merchant does not make a legal warranty that this transaction cannot be avoided, subordinated, or challenged under bankruptcy, fraudulent-transfer, preference, or other law. No such challenge or avoidance itself creates an Event of Default or liability under the Guaranty.
current_body: Merchant’s execution of and performance under this Agreement will not cause or create an event of default by Merchant under any contract with another person or entity, nor will it be considered a fraudulent transfer or fraudulent conveyance, or otherwise be void or voidable under similar laws or principles, the doctrine of equitable subordination, laws regarding preferential transfers, or for any other reason.
my_note: With 045. A merchant cannot warrant judicial conclusions about fraudulent transfer, preference or equitable subordination — outcomes that turn partly on OUR conduct and the value we gave. Replace with disclosure of known contractual restrictions.

heading: Indemnification
memo_rationale: This independently makes guarantors liable for every default and servicer claim, bypassing §9.2, and attempts to accrue statutory interest from demand. Limit indemnity to third-party losses caused by specified misconduct; first-party collection stays in §6.
memo_replacement:
Merchant shall indemnify Buyer only for the portion of a third-party claim finally determined by a court, or resolved in a written settlement approved by Merchant, to have been directly caused by Merchant’s fraud or intentional diversion of Purchased Receipts. Buyer shall give prompt notice, reasonably cooperate, and permit a defense by competent counsel. No settlement may impose an admission or nonmonetary duty on Buyer or fail to release it without Buyer’s consent, not unreasonably withheld. Delayed notice reduces liability only to the extent of material prejudice.
This indemnity excludes Buyer’s or its representatives’ negligence, fraud, willful misconduct, or legal violation; penalties imposed for their conduct; ordinary failure of future receipts to arise; and first-party claims governed by Section 6.2. It creates no independent Guarantor liability. Costs and interest remain subject to Section 6.3, no amount increases the purchased balance or split, and no loss may be recovered twice.
current_body: Upon the occurrence of any Event of Default, Merchant and Guarantor(s) jointly and severally shall assume liability for and hereby agree to indemnify, protect, and keep harmless Buyer and any third-party servicers from and against any and all liabilities, claims, losses, obligations, damages, penalties, actions, and suits of whatsoever kind and nature imposed on, incurred by, or asserted against Buyer or any third-party servicers in any way relating to or arising out of such Event of Default (collectively, “Indemnified Amounts”), including, subject to the aggregate limit in Section 6.3, the payment of costs and expenses reasonably incurred for the enforcement of Buyer’s rights and remedies hereunder, including the collection of amounts due to Buyer hereunder and attorneys’ fees and costs in any trial court or appellate court proceeding or administrative proceeding, or any negotiations or consultations, in connection with any Event of Default. Such Indemnified Amounts shall accrue at the rate set forth in Section 6.3.1, from the date of demand until paid in full.
my_note: Critical and correctly rated. §7.9 makes guarantors liable for every default and every servicer claim, which simply bypasses the limited guaranty in §9.2. Third-party losses caused by specified misconduct only; first-party collection stays in §6.

heading: Guaranty of Performance
memo_rationale: The express no-repayment/business-failure exclusions are important, but liability for any materially inaccurate present-fact representation is not limited to knowing misconduct. Combined with §§5.11/5.13 it can guarantee unknowable facts. The replacement adopts a narrower bad-act guaranty tied to the guarantor’s own conduct and proved causation; this is a conservative allocation beyond what every NY court requires. [A1–A4]
memo_replacement:
Each person separately signing as Guarantor is liable only for proven direct loss caused by fraud in connection with this Agreement that the Guarantor personally committed or knowingly directed, or intentional diversion of Purchased Receipts actually generated that the Guarantor personally committed or knowingly directed to prevent delivery to Buyer (the “Guaranteed Obligations”). An inaccurate representation alone does not establish fraud. Buyer bears the burden of proving the specified conduct, causation, and loss.
This is not a guaranty of the full Purchased Amount, future receipts, business performance, or every covenant. Insufficient receipts, slowdown, good-faith closure or failure, insolvency, bankruptcy, avoidance or clawback, a technical breach, or default under another agreement does not itself create liability. Liability is limited to proven direct loss from the specified conduct and costs permitted by Section 6.3, with credit for all recoveries for the same loss. No other clause or incorporated document expands this Guaranty. Buyer shall give Guarantor written notice describing the claim and supporting facts and enforce it only through lawful process or a written settlement.
current_body: The undersigned Guarantor(s) hereby guarantee to {{funder}} (“Buyer”) only the following, and nothing else in this Agreement (the “Guaranteed Obligations”): (a) that Merchant has not committed fraud in connection with this Agreement; (b) that no representation or warranty of present fact made by Merchant in this Agreement was incorrect, false or misleading in any material respect when made, other than any representation as to Merchant’s future intentions, anticipations or expectations; and (c) that Merchant has not acted with the intent to interfere with Buyer’s right to collect the Receipts purchased under this Agreement, including by the conduct described in Section 5.17 or Section 6.1.8. This Guaranty does not guarantee the repayment of the Receipts, the performance of any other covenant in this Agreement, or Merchant’s business performance. For the avoidance of doubt, no Guarantor has any liability under this Guaranty arising from a decline in Merchant’s sales, the cessation or failure of Merchant’s business, Merchant’s insolvency, or any bankruptcy filing by or against Merchant. Guarantor’s obligations are due at the time of any breach by Merchant of any of the Guaranteed Obligations under this Agreement.
my_note: Critical and correct. The express no-repayment and business-failure exclusions are the best thing in this document and must survive. What must go is liability for any materially inaccurate present-fact representation — unqualified by knowledge — which via §§5.11/5.13 guarantees facts a guarantor cannot know. Narrow to the guarantor's own conduct with proved causation.

heading: Guarantor Waivers
memo_rationale: The bankruptcy-clawback reinstatement directly conflicts with §§6.1/9.2. Unconsented renewals/amendments and impairment waivers can broaden the guaranty beyond its stated purpose. Preserve direct suit on a valid limited claim, but remove automatic expansion and permanent defense waivers. [A19]
memo_replacement:
Subject to Section 9.2, Buyer need not first obtain judgment against Merchant or realize upon Collateral before bringing a valid claim against Guarantor. No renewal, additional purchase, material amendment, substituted obligation, or increase in the Purchased Amount binds Guarantor without that Guarantor’s separate written consent identifying the resulting obligation. A notice of termination or nonrenewal does not itself create default or liability. It prevents extension of this Guaranty to any later transaction but does not release liability for conduct independently covered by Section 9.2 in this identified transaction; no future transaction is covered without fresh signed consent.
Guarantor retains defenses concerning validity, scope, causation, amount, payment, and all non-waivable rights. Subrogation, reimbursement, and contribution are postponed only while their exercise would cause duplicate recovery or materially impair recovery of a valid unpaid Guaranteed Obligation; they are not permanently waived. A payment returned or avoided in bankruptcy does not enlarge or reinstate this Guaranty. Bankruptcy-related events create no liability without independently proven conduct covered by Section 9.2. All enforcement remains subject to applicable stays and law.
current_body:
In the event that Merchant breaches any of the Guaranteed Obligations, Buyer may enforce its rights under this Guaranty without first seeking to obtain payment from Merchant, any other guarantor, or any Collateral or Additional Collateral Buyer may hold pursuant to this Guaranty. Buyer does not have to notify Guarantor of any of the following events, and Guarantor will not be released from its obligations under this Guaranty if it is not notified of: (i) Buyer’s failure to receive in a timely manner any amount due under this Agreement; (ii) any adverse change in Merchant’s financial condition or business; (iii) any sale or other disposition of any collateral securing the Guaranteed Obligations; (iv) Buyer’s acceptance of this Guaranty; and (v) any renewal, extension, or other modification of this Agreement.
In addition, Buyer may take any of the following actions without releasing Guarantor: (i) renew, extend, or otherwise modify this Agreement; (ii) release Merchant from its obligations to Buyer; (iii) sell, release, impair, waive, or otherwise fail to realize upon any collateral securing the Guaranteed Obligations; and (iv) foreclose on any collateral in a manner that impairs or precludes Guarantor’s right to obtain reimbursement.
Until the Purchased Amount and all other amounts payable under this Agreement have been received by Buyer in full, Guarantor shall not seek reimbursement from Merchant or any other guarantor for any amounts paid by it under this Guaranty. Guarantor waives and shall not seek to exercise any of the following rights against Merchant, any other guarantor, or any collateral provided by Merchant or any other guarantor for any amounts paid by it, or acts performed by it, under this Guaranty: (i) subrogation; (ii) reimbursement; (iii) performance; (iv) indemnification; or (v) contribution. In the event that Buyer must return any amount paid by Merchant or any other guarantor because that person has become subject to a proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code or any similar law, Guarantor’s obligations under this Guaranty shall include that amount.
my_note: Critical. The bankruptcy-clawback reinstatement in §9.4 directly contradicts §§6.1 and 9.2 and is the third route around the limited guaranty. Combined with 065 and 085, these three clauses are one fix and must land together or the leak simply moves.

heading: Joint and Several Liability
memo_rationale: Joint-and-several language is not inherently invalid, but it cannot bind absent signatories. Under the proposed own-conduct guaranty, one guarantor should not pay for another’s unrelated acts. Preserve joint liability only for the same loss caused by each person’s covered conduct.
memo_replacement: Each Guarantor’s liability is determined separately under Section 9.2. Guarantors may be jointly and severally liable only for the same proven loss caused by conduct independently covered by each one’s signed Guaranty, and Buyer may recover that loss only once. No person is liable merely because another Guarantor signed or committed a wrongful act.
current_body: The obligations of the persons or entities constituting Guarantors under this Guaranty are joint and several.
my_note: Joint and several cannot bind an absent signatory, and under an own-conduct guaranty one guarantor should not answer for another's unrelated act. Preserve joint liability only for the same loss.

heading: Guarantor Acknowledgement
memo_rationale: The opportunity-to-consult acknowledgement is appropriate. Tie the signature to the precise limited guaranty and remove any implication that actual attorney review is mandatory or occurred.
memo_replacement: Each Guarantor acknowledges receiving Sections 9.1 through 9.6 and the complete Agreement, understanding that Section 9.2 creates limited personal or entity liability for specified conduct, and having a reasonable opportunity to ask questions and consult independent counsel. Guarantor may choose not to consult counsel. This acknowledgement does not expand liability or waive defenses or statutory rights.
current_body: Guarantor acknowledges (i) the seriousness of the provisions of this Guaranty, and (ii) has had a full opportunity to consult with counsel of its choice or has decided not to avail himself or herself of that opportunity.
my_note: Tie the acknowledgement to the precise limited guaranty and stop implying counsel was actually consulted.

memo_rationale: Delete the separate guarantor waiver; §10.1 applies to every party and guarantor.
current_body: Guarantor hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waives personal service of any summons, complaint, or other process, which may be made by any other means permitted by New York or Florida law. Guarantor further agrees to waive any objection to the absence of formal service of process.
my_note: Delete; §10.1 covers every party and guarantor. Pure duplication.

memo_rationale: Delete for the same reason as §10.3; separate Guarantor contact data belongs in §9.1 and ordinary notices.
current_body: GUARANTOR HEREBY AGREES TO ACCEPT SERVICE OF ANY SUMMONS, COMPLAINT, OR OTHER PROCESS BY ELECTRONIC MAIL AT _____________«50»_____________ OR BY UNITED STATES POSTAL SERVICE AT ____________________________«51»____________________________ OR BY ANY OTHER MEANS PERMITTED BY NEW YORK OR FLORIDA LAW.
my_note: Delete for the same reason as 092. Guarantor contact data belongs in §9.1, which is the clause we currently cannot see.
